source.title_on_document: The Effects of Dual-Pathway AI Assistance on Divergent Thinking in Tasks of Varying Semantic Richness

paper_design_summary: In one within-subjects experiment, 35 participants did the Alternative Uses Task for semantically rich and semantically sparse objects under three conditions: flexible AI (cues for cross-category exploration), persistent AI (cues for within-category deepening), and a no-AI baseline. In a turn-taking brainstorming paradigm, the AI gave a tailored cue after each idea from the participant. The paper scores the originality of the ideas; the abstract does not say whether the order of conditions was randomized or how originality was scored.

one_line_finding: In a within-subjects AUT study (N = 35), persistent AI increased mean originality only for semantically rich tasks, no overall mean-originality benefit was evident for flexible AI on semantically sparse tasks, and both AI conditions elevated initial originality across both task types (OpenAlex abstract, sentences 3 and 5-7; no numeric effect estimates or inferential statistics in the abstract).

applied.old: With N = 35 in a within-subjects AUT design, persistent AI raised mean originality only for semantically rich objects, flexible AI did not raise mean originality, and both AI conditions raised initial originality (abstract, OpenAlex record; no numbers in the abstract).
